answer: After a tax lien has been held long enough, the lawful holder of the certificate of purchase may apply for a treasurer's deed; the county treasurer then holds a public auction, and the winning bidder receives a certificate of option for a treasurer's deed.
quote: AFTER AUGUST 1 OF THE THIRD CALENDAR YEAR FOLLOWING THE DATE OF A TAX LIEN SALE, A LAWFUL HOLDER MAY APPLY FOR A TREASURER'S DEED FOR THE PROPERTY DESCRIBED IN THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ... "CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED" MEANS A CERTIFICATE ISSUED BY A TREASURER TO THE SUCCESSFUL PURCHASER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

answer: The first public auction must be scheduled no less than 30 and no more than 60 calendar days after the treasurer mails the notice of public auction.
quote: THE INITIAL PUBLIC AUCTION HELD PURSUANT TO THIS ARTICLE 11.5 MUST BE SCHEDULED FOR NO LESS THAN THIRTY CALENDAR DAYS NOR MORE THAN SIXTY CALENDAR DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF MAILING THE NOTICE OF PUBLIC AUCTION.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

answer: The treasurer holds the public auction at a courthouse or at a building housing the county clerk and recorder or the treasurer, as named in the notice; it may also be held on the internet or another electronic medium.
quote: THE TREASURER SHALL CONDUCT THE PUBLIC AUCTION AT ANY DOOR OR ENTRANCE TO, OR IN ANY ROOM IN ANY BUILDING TEMPORARILY OR PERMANENTLY USED AS, A COURTHOUSE OR AT OR WITHIN ANY BUILDING WHERE THE OFFICE OF THE COUNTY CLERK AND RECORDER OR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER IS LOCATED, WHICH PLACE MUST BE SPECIFICALLY DESIGNATED IN THE NOTICE OF PUBLIC AUCTION; EXCEPT THAT A PUBLIC AUCTION MAY ALSO BE CONDUCTED BY MEANS OF THE INTERNET OR OTHER ELECTRONIC MEDIUM.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

answer: The statutory notice of public auction tells interested bidders that they must register and gives the treasurer's website or office phone number for more information.
quote: INTERESTED BIDDERS MUST REGISTER. MORE INFORMATION AT (WEBSITE OR TREASURER'S OFFICE PHONE NUMBER).
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 lets the treasurer require a deposit from the lawful holder applying for a deed (39-11.5-102(5)); no statewide bidder deposit was found. Check the county treasurer's bidding rules.

answer: The lawful holder must bid no less than the total debt as determined by the treasurer; the bid form sets out all money due to the lawful holder, including the treasurer's fees and costs.
quote: MUST SET FORTH ALL MONEY DUE AND OWING TO THE LAWFUL HOLDER, INCLUDING ALL TREASURER FEES AND COSTS ... A LAWFUL HOLDER MUST BID NO LESS THAN THE AMOUNT OF THE TOTAL DEBT, AS DETERMINED BY THE TREASURER, FOR THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE BEING SOLD.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

answer: Payment of the amount bid must reach the treasurer by the date and time of the auction, or at another time on the auction day that the treasurer sets in writing, in the form the treasurer specifies. If the highest bidder does not pay in full, the next highest bidder who pays in time is the successful bidder.
quote: THE PAYMENT OF ANY AMOUNT BID AT AN AUCTION MUST BE RECEIVED BY A TREASURER NO LATER THAN THE DATE AND TIME OF THE AUCTION, OR AT AN ALTERNATIVE TIME AFTER THE AUCTION AND ON THE DAY OF THE AUCTION, AS SPECIFIED IN WRITING BY THE TREASURER. A BID PAYMENT MUST BE MADE IN THE FORM SPECIFIED BY THE TREASURER.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

answer: If the property is sold to a third-party bidder, or to the lawful holder bidding competitively, the treasurer may collect up to $300 from the successful bidder for processing the public auction.
quote: IF A PROPERTY IS SOLD TO A THIRD-PARTY BIDDER OR A LAWFUL HOLDER AS A COMPETITIVE BIDDER, A TREASURER MAY COLLECT UP TO THREE HUNDRED DOLLARS FROM THE SUCCESSFUL BIDDER FOR PERFORMING ACTIONS RELATED TO PROCESSING THE PUBLIC AUCTION
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

answer: The property owner may redeem before the auction by filing an intent to redeem no later than seven calendar days before the scheduled auction. After the auction, a lawful holder who did not win may repurchase the certificate of option by noon on the eighth business day after the auction.
quote: A PROPERTY OWNER IS ENTITLED TO REDEEM A PROPERTY IF, NO LATER THAN SEVEN CALENDAR DAYS PRIOR TO THE CURRENTLY SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION DATE, THE PROPERTY OWNER FILES AN INTENT TO REDEEM ... NO LATER THAN NOON ON THE EIGHTH BUSINESS DAY FOLLOWING THE PUBLIC AUCTION, THE LAWFUL HOLDER MAY REPURCHASE THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

answer: When the repurchase period ends, title vests in the holder of the certificate of option, and the treasurer executes and records a treasurer's deed confirming the transfer.
quote: UPON THE EXPIRATION OF THE REPURCHASE PERIOD ... TITLE TO THE PROPERTY VESTS IN THE HOLDER OF THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... THE TREASURER SHALL EXECUTE AND RECORD A TREASURER'S DEED PURSUANT TO SECTION 39-11.5-502 TO THE HOLDER OF THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... CONFIRMING THE TRANSFER OF TITLE TO THE PROPERTY.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

answer: Subject to junior lienors' overbid claims, title is free and clear of liens and encumbrances junior to the certificate of purchase. The treasurer's deed does not affect existing roads, rights-of-way, conservation easements, other easements or equitable servitudes.
quote: THE TITLE IS FREE AND CLEAR OF ALL LIENS AND ENCUMBRANCES JUNIOR TO THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ... EXECUTION OF A TREASURER'S DEED PURSUANT TO THIS SECTION DOES NOT AFFECT THE EXISTENCE OF ANY PUBLIC OR PRIVATE ROADS, RIGHTS-OF-WAY, CONSERVATION EASEMENTS, OTHER EASEMENTS, OR EQUITABLE SERVITUDES
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

answer: If no valid bids are received at the public auction, the lawful holder who does not withdraw the application becomes the purchaser.
quote: "PURCHASER" MEANS A PERSON TO WHOM THE TREASURER AWARDS THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED AS THE WINNING BIDDER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION WHO TIMELY SUBMITS PROPER FUNDS, OR, IF NO VALID BIDS ARE RECEIVED AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION, THE LAWFUL HOLDER WHO DOES NOT FILE A WITHDRAWAL OF THE APPLICATION
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: No statewide statutory due-diligence instruction to buyers was found; county treasurers' pages carry 'buyer beware' warnings (see county rows).

answer: The treasurer prepares a certificate of purchase for the purchaser of a tax lien on real property sold for delinquent taxes; it describes the property and states the rate of interest and the total taxes, delinquent interest and fees.
quote: The treasurer shall prepare, sign, and retain for safekeeping or deliver to the purchaser of a tax lien on any real property sold for the payment of delinquent taxes a certificate of purchase describing the property on which the taxes and fees were paid by the purchaser, as the same was described in the record of sales, and also stating the rate of interest and the total amount of all taxes, delinquent interest, and fees
source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
note: SB 26-144 amended 39-11-117 (wording only); quoted words are unchanged.

answer: Tax liens are sold to the bidders who pay the taxes, delinquent interest and fees, or who pay the largest amount above them (a premium); the excess goes to the county general fund.
quote: sold to the persons who pay therefor the taxes, delinquent interest, and fees then due thereon or who further pay the largest amount in excess of said taxes, delinquent interest, and fees. The excess amount shall be credited to the county general fund.
source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
note: SB 26-144 amended 39-11-115(1): 'shall' became 'MUST' in the last sentence; the rule is otherwise unchanged.

answer: Redemption interest is nine percentage points above the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City discount rate, rounded to the nearest full percent; the state banking commissioner sets it each September 1, effective October 1.
quote: The annual rate of redemption interest shall be nine percentage points above the discount rate, which discount rate shall be the rate of interest a commercial bank pays to the federal reserve bank of Kansas City using a government bond or other eligible paper as security, and shall be rounded to the nearest full percent.
source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
note: Read from the 2024 C.R.S. title 39 printout (the newest posted); SB 26-144 (2026) does not amend this section.

answer: The owner may redeem at any time before a treasurer's deed is executed. Under the treasurer's deed auction process, the owner must file an intent to redeem no later than seven calendar days before the scheduled auction.
quote: The redemption may be made at any time before the execution of a treasurer's deed ... A PROPERTY OWNER IS ENTITLED TO REDEEM A PROPERTY IF, NO LATER THAN SEVEN CALENDAR DAYS PRIOR TO THE CURRENTLY SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION DATE, THE PROPERTY OWNER FILES AN INTENT TO REDEEM THE PROPERTY WITH THE TREASURER.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: 39-12-103(3) quoted from the 2024 C.R.S. printout (https://leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/images/olls/crs2024-title-39.pdf), not amended by SB 26-144; 39-11.5-106 from the SB 26-144 session law.

answer: After August 1 of the third calendar year after the tax lien sale, the lawful holder may apply for a treasurer's deed. The property then goes to a public auction; if the holder is not the winning bidder, the holder may repurchase the certificate of option within the repurchase period.
quote: AFTER AUGUST 1 OF THE THIRD CALENDAR YEAR FOLLOWING THE DATE OF A TAX LIEN SALE, A LAWFUL HOLDER MAY APPLY FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... A LAWFUL HOLDER IS ENTITLED TO REPURCHASE A CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED IF THE FOLLOWING REQUIREMENTS ARE MET TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE TREASURER: (a) THE LAWFUL HOLDER WAS NOT THE SUCCESSFUL PURCHASER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

answer: A certificate of purchase lien may not remain a lien longer than seven years after issuance (the rule does not apply to certificates held by the county). A certificate issued before January 1, 2026 may remain a lien for fifteen years.
quote: No lien upon property created by a certificate of purchase issued by a treasurer on account of any delinquent property taxes or any special assessment MAY remain a lien for a period longer than SEVEN years after the issuance thereof ... NOTWITHSTANDING ANY OTHER PROVISION OF THIS SECTION, A LIEN ON PROPERTY CREATED BY A TAX LIEN SALE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 1, 2026, MAY REMAIN A LIEN FOR A PERIOD OF FIFTEEN YEARS AFTER THE DATE OF ISSUANCE.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: As amended by SB 26-144: the session law strikes 'fifteen' and adds 'SEVEN'; quoted with struck words omitted (read from the printed page).

answer: The Morgan County Treasurer (who also serves as Public Trustee) handles tax lien sales and treasurer's deed auctions: P.O. Box 593, Fort Morgan, CO 80701, phone 970-542-3518, Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.
quote: County Treasurer Robert A. Sagel ... P.O. Box 593 Fort Morgan, CO 80701 970-542-3518 ... Office Hours Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
source_title: Treasurer and Public Trustee | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky

answer: Treasurer's deed option auctions are held on Wednesdays at 9:30 a.m.; auction dates are on the published notice and the Treasurer's website.
quote: Auctions are conducted on Wednesdays at 9:30 a.m. ... Auction dates can be found on the published notice and the Treasurer's website.
source_title: Bidding Rules and Information | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky
note: Page title: 'Auction for Certificate of Option for a Treasurer's Deed Bidding Rules and Information'. The page predates or does not cite SB 26-144; check it against the current statute.

answer: Auctions are held in person at the east front door of the Morgan County Administration Building; the Treasurer takes verbal bids from registered bidders or their agents who are present, in $5.00 minimum increments.
quote: at the east front door of the Morgan County Administration Building ... the Treasurer will entertain verbal bids from any registered bidders or their designated agents that are present. The minimum bid increment is $5.00.
source_title: Bidding Rules and Information | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky

answer: All bidders must register with the Morgan County Treasurer's office before the auction.
quote: All bidders must register with the Morgan County Treasurer's office prior to the auction
source_title: Bidding Rules and Information | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky

answer: The winning bid must be paid to the Morgan County Treasurer by noon on the sale day, in cash, cashier's check payable to the Morgan County Treasurer, bank check, or electronic transfer to an account the Treasurer specifies. If the highest bidder has not paid by noon, the next highest bidder who has paid in full by 2:00 p.m. is the successful bidder.
quote: Payment of any successful bid amount must be received by the Morgan County Treasurer no later than noon on the same day as the sale. If full payment of the bid amount from the highest bidder at the sale is not received by noon on the day of the sale, the next highest bidder who has tendered the full amount of their bid by 2:00 p.m. on the day of the auction shall be deemed the successful bidder
source_title: Bidding Rules and Information | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky
note: Accepted funds (same page): cash, a Cashier's Check payable to the Morgan County Treasurer, a bank check, or by electronic transfer to an account specified by the Treasurer.

answer: Morgan County's tax lien sale is a premium auction held online: the bidder offering the highest premium above the tax lien buys it; the minimum premium is $1.00 and successful premium bids are not refunded.
quote: A premium bid is an amount over and above the tax lien being offered. Minimum premium bids are $1.00. If there are competing bids, the investor offering the highest premium bid purchases the tax lien. PLEASE BE AWARE THAT SUCCESSFUL PREMIUM BIDS ARE NOT REFUNDED.
source_title: Tax Lien Sale | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky
note: The page describes the 2025 sale (online at zeusauction.com, November 18-20, 2025). Unsold liens are held by the county and are normally available from the Treasurer's office (same page).

answer: The Saguache County Treasurer/Public Trustee handles tax lien sales and treasurer's deed auctions: PO Box 177, Saguache, CO 81149, phone 719-655-2656, email saguachetreasurer@saguachecounty-co.gov.
quote: For inquires and general information: saguachetreasurer@saguachecounty-co.gov ... PO Box 177 Saguache, CO 81149 Phone: 719-655-2656
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County

answer: The annual tax lien auction will be held online November 2-4, 2026. Treasurer's deed auctions are held online every two weeks on Wednesdays at 10am, except holidays.
quote: Annual Tax Lien Auction will be held online, November 2-4, 2026. ... All Treasurer's Deed auctions will be held bi-weekly on Wednesday's at 10am, with the exception of holidays online
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County
note: The Saguache records on this site come from the County's 2026 tax lien sale list.

answer: The tax lien sale for real properties and minerals is online only, at zeusauction.com. Treasurer's deed auctions are online at GovEase; a workstation is available in the Treasurer's office.
quote: Real properties and Mineral Interest will be online only. ... All Treasurer's Deed auctions will be held bi-weekly on Wednesday's at 10am, with the exception of holidays online at; https://liveauctions.govease.com/co/cosaguachetread/1418/browsestandard ... A workstation is available in the Treasurer's office
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County

answer: Bidders register for the tax lien sale at zeusauction.com. For treasurer's deed auctions you must create a GovEase account and also register for the specific auction.
quote: Saguache County Tax Lien Sale accepts registration for bidders at www.zeusauction.com. ... You will need to create an account and register for the auction. Creating an account with GovEase.com will not automatically register you for an auction
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County

answer: For treasurer's deed auctions, bids are paid by wire transfer through the auction company.
quote: 3-Bids will be paid via wire transfer through the auction company.
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County
note: Treasurer's deed auction bidding rules; the page states no payment terms for the annual tax lien sale.

answer: For treasurer's deed auctions, any current year's tax not endorsed before the auction is the responsibility of the party who receives the treasurer's deed.
quote: Any current year's tax that was not endorsed prior to the auction will be the responsibility of the parties to whom the Treasurer's Deed is issued.
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County

answer: The Douglas County Treasurer's office handles the tax lien sale, county-held liens and treasurer's deeds: phone 303-660-7455, general information 303-660-7400.
quote: If you want to assign your purchase to another investor, contact our office at 303.660.7455 ... Treasurer Phone: 303-660-7455 ... General Info 303-660-7400
source_title: Tax Lien Sale Information - Douglas County

answer: Douglas County's 2026 internet tax lien sale is held November 5, 2026 through zeusauction.com. It is a premium auction: the minimum starting bid is the delinquent taxes, interest, advertising and fees, and bidders may bid above it; premiums are never returned and draw no interest.
quote: The 2026 Internet Tax Lien Sale will be held Nov 5th, 2026 ... The minimum starting bid for each tax lien certificate is equal to the amount of the delinquent taxes, interest, advertising and fees as shown on the SRI internet auction website. Douglas County tax certificates sales are "PREMIUM" auctions in which a bidder can choose to bid up the minimum amount due. Premiums are never returned and draw no interest
source_title: Tax Lien Sale Information - Douglas County
note: Same page: 2026 interest is 13%; payment for winning bids is by ACH from the bank account given at registration.
